name: Hiwonder MentorPi T1
description: A Raspberry Pi 5, ROS2 Humble tracked robot with a genuine structured-light depth camera and 2D LiDAR for SLAM — the tank-tread member of Hiwonder's MentorPi family, alongside the Ackermann-steered A1 and Mecanum-wheel M1. A real, budget-tier alternative to TurtleBot4 or Yahboom ROSMASTER for the same use case, at roughly half to a third of TurtleBot4's price.

sourcing: Specs compiled from Hiwonder's own product and documentation pages and GitHub repository as of this build. The LiDAR's exact range/accuracy specs and the T1 chassis's dimensions, weight, and payload capacity were not independently verifiable — confirm before purchase.

pricing.summary: Hiwonder's own site lists a base configuration from $329.99; RobotShop carries a Starter Kit (Pi 5, 4GB) at $599.99 up to a Standard Kit (Pi 5, 16GB) at $977.99, with an Advanced tier also listed on Amazon. Realistic buy-in for a functional kit runs roughly $600–$1,000 depending on configuration — well under TurtleBot4's current $1,500–$2,000+ price range for a comparable ROS2/SLAM/depth-camera setup, and in the same bracket as Yahboom ROSMASTER.

editorial.heading: Insights
editorial.body: Hiwonder's MentorPi GitHub repository contains real, substantial ROS2 packages (SLAM, navigation, YOLO vision), but it has no LICENSE file, so no Open Source badge is applied here — the same situation as this catalog's Yahboom ROSMASTER entry. A published review of the sibling A1 chassis, which shares the same electronics and software stack, found its unit shipped with a default firmware configuration that didn't match the ordered variant and required manual reconfiguration, a plausible risk worth watching for on T1 as well.
